member.name: T:geoDC.Application.Abstractions.Crs.ITransformationGridStore
member.summary: The transformation grids geoDC knows: the ones bundled with the application, and the ones the user downloads, or imports from a file, into their own grid folder. Every grid comes from one pinned PROJ-data release and is checked against its SHA-256 before it is installed.
member.remarks: Installing or removing a grid does not change a strict transformation's result. PROJ rates its best operation as if every grid were installed, so without the grid that operation is refused, not replaced. Only refusals become results. Downloads, imports and removals run one at a time, and listing can run alongside them.

member.summary: The single boundary through which data-series rows change: values, inclusion, tags and restores. member.summary: Computes what would change, without changing anything.

member.name: M:geoDC.Application.Abstractions.DataSeries.IDataSeriesEditSession.Apply(geoDC.Application.DataSeries.DataSeriesEditPreview)
member.summary: Applies the previewed changes, and only those, after rechecking the version, the consumers and each row's before state. A refusal leaves every row unchanged.

member.name: M:geoDC.Application.Abstractions.DataSeries.IDataSeriesEditSession.CreateWorkingCopy(NUlid.Ulid)
member.summary: Copies the series into a new, independent series in the same job, so data that locked work protects can be corrected without changing that work's evidence. The copy gets new series and row identities and keeps the rows' current keys, values, inclusion, tags and recorded originals. No attempt is retargeted: the source and everything that uses it stay as they are. Recorded as one undo step.
member.returns: The copy's identity, or null when the series is unknown.

member.summary: Asks once to reopen the locked work that uses the series, so its rows can be edited. The confirmation lists that work and everything that depends on it. Reopened work keeps its calculation until an edit changes the rows it uses, and its reports become invalid.
member.returns: Whether the work was reopened. False when nothing locked uses the series or the request was dismissed.

member.name: T:geoDC.Application.Abstractions.Ingestion.ITextIngestor
member.summary: Reads delimited text held in memory, such as points pasted into an import, through the same row parsing and column mapping as a CSV file.

remarks.para: Delimiter detection samples the first 50 non-blank lines. It picks the first of tab, semicolon and comma that splits every sampled line into the same number of fields (at least two), and then tries whitespace on the same terms. If none does, it picks the first that splits every sampled line into at least two fields. If none does that either, it uses comma, which reads each line as one column. Whitespace is preferred to comma when both split every line evenly and each comma left inside a whitespace-separated field sits between digits, as in P1 1,5 2,5 3,0.

For comma-separated text, the detected decimal separator is a point. Otherwise detection looks at the fields made only of digits, points and commas, and applies these rules in order. If a field holds both a point and a comma, the later one is the decimal separator. If there are commas but no points, it is a decimal comma. If points and commas appear in separate fields, it is a decimal point when every comma groups thousands (1,000), and a decimal comma otherwise. In any other case it is a point.

A detected header row is a first line with a non-numeric value in a column that is numeric on every later sampled line, reading numbers as the rows are parsed. A single line is a header only when none of its values is numeric.

member.summary: Finds the formats that read the most of , one per distinct reading, best first. Passing a format back as the parse options' date-time format reads every row the same way.
member.remarks: Formats that read the values to the same times are one reading. Readings differ where the text is ambiguous, as when every day is 12 or less and the day and month could swap. Readings whose times run forwards over the shortest span rank first, and ISO 8601 and day-before-month break a tie.

member.name: T:geoDC.Application.Abstractions.Mapping.IMapTileStore
member.summary: Map tiles by zoom, column and row in the XYZ ("slippy map") scheme, from a disk cache in front of the configured tile server (). Tiles are for display only: nothing a tile shows feeds a report, a calculation or a project fingerprint.

remarks.para: A cached tile is served while it is fresh. An older one is fetched again, and kept if the fetch fails, so a map that loaded once still draws without a connection. The cache is kept within by removing the tiles used least recently. A size of 0 keeps nothing.
Tiles are fetched only as the map asks for them, not in bulk, with the application's own user agent, as public tile servers' usage policies ask. Each tile server has its own part of the cache.

member.name: T:geoDC.Application.Alterations.AlterationGuard
member.summary: Owns confirmation, single-use tokens and the recorded baseline for one workspace lifetime. Hosts call it on their serialised workspace thread.
member.remarks: Every check reconciles the live workspace with the recorded baseline. A change that reaches only unfinalised work is accepted and invalidates the calculations it affects, whether or not a token recorded it. A change that reaches finalised work without an accepted confirmation leaves that work untouched and lists it as changed finalised work until the change is restored or the work is reopened, which then invalidates its calculation. Only a failure while applying consequences blocks the guard.

member.name: T:geoDC.Application.Calibration.ShoreControlGridConvergence
member.summary: Computes the grid convergence a heading calibration applies from the job's Shore Control: the meridian convergence of the projected CRS its active points are stated in, at their mean position, through .
member.remarks: The control-point data is positioned from the Shore Control, so its grid is the Shore Control's. Data Defined in another CRS is refused, not corrected with another grid's convergence. Points in a geographic CRS or without a defined CRS are left out. An epoch is ignored, because convergence is a property of the projection. Across a dock the convergence changes by well under a thousandth of a degree, so one value at the mean position serves the job.

member.name: T:geoDC.Application.Charting.VrfFeaturePoint
member.summary: A feature placed in the VRF scene. X/Y/Z are the stored VRF offsets in metres, in GEOdc Standard axes (+X forward, +Y starboard, +Z down). Type is the lower-cased FeatureType token (e.g. "sensor-mount" / "structure-point" / "poi"). IsOrigin flags the Common Reference Point (always at 0,0,0). Measured distinguishes captured states from planned ones, and Drift marks a measured position whose drift waits for a decision, so the scene can colour it and always label it.

member.name: T:geoDC.Application.Charting.ChartRegionSelection
member.summary: Payload of the generic "regionSelect" a brush-mode chart raises when the user finishes sweeping a region. Bounds are in data space. X0/X1 are always set, and Y0/Y1 are null for a one-dimensional brush. XIsTime repeats whether the x bounds are epoch milliseconds. Ids are the source-row keys of the marks inside the region. The chart fills them in so a consumer can act on rows directly without hit-testing the geometry again. An empty Ids with null bounds means the selection was cleared. Modifier is the modifier key held ("shift" or "alt", otherwise null), so a consumer can tell add, remove and replace apart.

member.name: T:geoDC.Application.Charting.IChartDataAssembler
member.summary: Turns approved domain results into renderer-neutral chart DTOs. It lives in Application so the interactive host and the report path build figures the same way.
member.remarks:
Two principles hold throughout:
Statistics are authoritative. Mean, sigma, min and max are copied from the domain COStatistic, and the chart does not recompute them, so the figure cannot disagree with the approved value.
The convention is required context. The calculation SignConvention.Name is passed through so the C-O axis can show which convention it is in.

member.name: M:geoDC.Application.Charting.IChartDataAssembler.BuildVerificationHistogram(geoDC.Domain.Verification.DisplayedVerificationResult,System.String,System.Decimal)
member.summary: Builds the residual histogram for a computed verification result in the display convention it is shown in: the residual samples in degrees, with the result's mean and sigma copied through as the authoritative overlays. is the maximum absolute mean in degrees, drawn as symmetric ± guides. It is not a per-sample limit.

member.name: M:geoDC.Application.Charting.IChartDataAssembler.BuildCo(geoDC.Domain.Calibration.DisplayedCalibrationResult,geoDC.Domain.DataSeries.DataSeries{geoDC.Measurements.Angle},System.String)
member.summary: Builds the C-O figure from a computed calibration result in the display convention it is shown in, and the observed angle series it was differenced against, in the same convention. Calibration has no acceptance criteria (that is a verification concern), so is left null.

member.name: M:geoDC.Application.Charting.IChartDataAssembler.BuildVerificationResidual(geoDC.Domain.Verification.DisplayedVerificationResult,geoDC.Domain.DataSeries.DataSeries{geoDC.Measurements.Angle},System.String,System.String,System.Decimal,System.Decimal)
member.summary: Builds the residual figure for a computed verification result in the display convention it is shown in, on the same C-O chart a calibration uses: the residual series named by , the computed and observed (post-application) angles it came from in the same convention, the result's statistics copied through, and the acceptance limits in degrees. The acceptance guides sit at ±. They bound the mean, not individual samples.

member.name: M:geoDC.Application.Charting.IChartDataAssembler.BuildSeries(geoDC.Domain.DataSeries.DataSeries{geoDC.Measurements.Angle},System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Builds a simple value-over-time figure from an angle series (e.g. an imported observed dataset), for the optional offscreen-rendered preview.

member.name: M:geoDC.Application.Charting.IChartDataAssembler.BuildGnss(geoDC.Domain.GnssCheck.GnssCheckAttemptResult,System.Nullable{System.Decimal},System.Nullable{System.Decimal},System.String)
member.summary: Builds the GNSS spot-check figure (ΔE/ΔN/ΔH per matched epoch) for the 3-D scatter. The tolerance ring/cylinder comes from the passed acceptance distances, or is absent when either limit is missing. The chart derives the covariance itself. The caption is , the frame the deltas were taken in, followed by the registered transformation steps that moved a series into it, e.g. geodc:etrf2000-utm31n (observed from EPSG:7912@2026.75 by EPSG:8405).

member.name: M:geoDC.Application.Charting.IChartDataAssembler.BuildVrf(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{geoDC.Application.Charting.VrfFeatureInput},geoDC.Domain.Common.Conventions.PositionConvention)
member.summary: Builds the interactive 3-D Vessel Reference Frame scene: the supplied features placed by their GEOdc Standard VRF offsets, with the axes named by the vessel's . The origin feature is always placed at (0,0,0). Other features are included only once they have a complete offset triple, so planned-only features without offsets are left out.

member.name: M:geoDC.Application.Charting.IChartDataAssembler.BuildVrfTransformPreview(geoDC.Application.VesselFrame.VrfTransformationReview,geoDC.Application.Abstractions.VesselFrame.VrfTransformationProposal)
member.summary: Builds the 3-D overlay for a transformation under review: the reviewer's after-positions (keyed by feature id, as the scene's feature points are), the proposal's nominated baselines, and its rotation. Positions are copied from , not recomputed.

member.name: M:geoDC.Application.Charting.IChartDataAssembler.BuildShoreControlPlan(geoDC.Domain.ShoreControl.ShoreControlSnapshot)
member.summary: Builds the plan view of a job's shore control snapshot in its set's default CRS: every live point whose current position is a grid easting and northing in that frame, at any epoch, with its status and horizontal uncertainty, and the earlier positions of those points in the same frame as superseded marks. Live points in another frame, or not projected, are listed in . Nothing is transformed. The caption gives the frame the name of the definition the snapshot holds, when it has one.

member.name: T:geoDC.Application.GnssCheck.GnssCheckCalculator
member.summary: The one path every GNSS check computation takes, for the app's in-memory workspace and the persistence-backed service alike. It settles the comparison with , transforms each series that is Defined in another CRS or epoch into the comparison frame through , and differences the result with . Positions are differenced without a transformation only when a series is Unspecified, and the comparison is then flagged as assumed.
member.remarks: Each coordinate is transformed at its series' epoch. A series in a static CRS transformed into a dynamic frame takes the frame's epoch. When the frame has no height axis, a transformed series keeps its own heights and the comparison says so (). A geocentric series cannot keep a height that way, so it is refused.

member.name: T:geoDC.Application.ShoreControl.ShoreControlPointImportPreview
member.summary: What importing a file of shore control points into one set would do, row by row. It is computed from the same rules the commit applies, without changing anything. Every row is read in one CRS reference (and its epoch), chosen once for the whole source. A name new to the set adds a point. A name that matches a live point appends a revision, unless the active revision already has the same coordinate and CRS reference, in which case the row is unchanged. An existing point's description and station type are left as they are. Rows that cannot be read are skipped with a .

member.name: T:geoDC.Application.VesselFrame.RigidTransformEntry
member.summary: Parses and validates an explicitly entered rigid transform. It accepts rigid transforms only, not general affine ones: values must be finite, a homogeneous final row must be [0, 0, 0, 1], and the rotation block must be orthonormal with determinant +1 (no scale, shear, or reflection). Numbers use the invariant culture, with a dot as the decimal separator, and may be separated by spaces, new lines, commas, semicolons, or brackets.

member.summary: Previews where each resolved feature state would move and lists every finding about the proposal. The result is blocked when, among other checks, the VRF is not established, nothing would move, the job has no resolved positions, a rotation would change completed dependent work, or a requested CRP assignment is not allowed. It does not throw for an invalid proposal. The findings say what is wrong.

member.name: T:geoDC.Reporting.Contracts.JobReport.ReportCalibration
member.summary: An INS calibration attempt in the job and, once computed, its C-O.
member.param: The attempt name.
An AngleSensorCapability member name.
The calibrated instrument's name, with its serial number in parentheses when it has one; empty when the instrument cannot be found.
An AttemptWorkflowStatus member name.
True when a later calibration attempt supersedes this one; the template greys the value and marks it not to be applied.
Who completed the attempt; null when not completed.
When the attempt was completed (ISO 8601 UTC); null when not completed.
Who approved the result; null when not approved.
When the result was approved (ISO 8601 UTC); null when not approved.
The calibration C-O; null when the attempt is not complete or could not be computed.
The C-O mean and σ in degrees and the sampled count, as computed in the calculation convention rather than re-expressed like ; null when no result is available.
True when the attempt is complete but its result could not be recomputed.
Root-relative path of the C-O chart, plotted in the calculation convention; null when none was rendered.

The prisms' VRF baseline angle the C-O was computed with, in degrees. For heading it is the bearing from CP1 to CP2 off the bow, clockwise. For pitch it is the tilt, positive when the forward prism is higher. For roll it is the tilt, positive when the port prism is higher. Null when no result is available.
